results.use_case: Analyze Salesforce opportunity pipeline data by discovering a custom field, retrieving stage metadata, querying filtered opportunity records, fetching stage-change history, and computing stage conversion and skip metrics.
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if field API names/history tracking are uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Inspect the target object schema using SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT (confirm the tracked stage/value/close-date fields and the correct field-history object).

[Optional (if you need a time-bounded or business-filtered cohort)] [Step]: Collect parent record IDs using SALESFORCE_GET_S_OBJECTS_UPDATED or SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY (IDs only) to constrain the history scan.

[Required] [Step]: Retrieve change rows using SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY on the relevant field-history object (select parent id, changed field, old/new values, change timestamp; filter to key fields and optional time window/parent IDs; ORDER BY change time).

[Required] [Next Step (if response data.done is false)]: Continue pagination by re-issuing SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY until data.done is true, concatenating data.records and optionally deduping per parent timeline.
[Optional (if you need typed/clean outputs)] [Step]: Normalize and post-filter old/new values using COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (null handling, numeric/date parsing, mixed-type safety).
[Fallback (if expected history rows are missing or visibility seems incomplete)] [Fallback]: Re-run the same history SOQL using SALESFORCE_QUERY_ALL.

[Optional (if current parent context is needed)] [Next Step]: Enrich distinct parent IDs using SALESFORCE_GET_OPPORTUNITY (small sets) or SALESFORCE_GET_A_BATCH_OF_RECORDS (larger sets) for rollups in COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH.
known_pitfalls: [SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Filtering on OldValue/NewValue in WHERE can fail with HTTP 400 INVALID_FIELD; fetch rows then filter client-side.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Incorrect or non-tracked field API names in history filters can yield totalSize=0 or HTTP 400 INVALID_FIELD.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] OR-heavy discovery queries can fail with HTTP 400 MALFORMED_QUERY; keep SOQL simple and rely on SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT for discovery.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Results are nested under data.records with completeness via data.done and sizing via data.totalSize; mis-parsing can silently drop rows.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Some history rows may have OldValue and NewValue both null; exclude these before summarizing “changes”.

toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=salesforce. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="salesforce") to create a connection BEFORE executing any salesforce tools.

SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY.description: Executes a SOQL query against Salesforce data. Returns records matching the query with pagination support.

examples: SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact WHERE CreatedDate > 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE Status = 'New'
SELECT COUNT(Id), StageName FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName
SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT Id, Name FROM Contact WHERE LastName = 'O\'Brien'
SELECT Id, Name, Description FROM Account LIMIT 10
query.description: SOQL query to execute. Must start with SELECT. Field names must match object schema exactly — use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT for unfamiliar objects. ALIASES: No 'AS' keyword (use 'SUM(Amount) TotalSales' NOT 'SUM(Amount) AS TotalSales'). AGGREGATES: Without GROUP BY, ORDER BY/LIMIT not allowed (single-row result). COUNT() SYNTAX: Bare COUNT() only valid alone. With GROUP BY or other fields, must specify field: COUNT(Id) or COUNT(fieldName). Example: 'SELECT COUNT(Id), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status' NOT 'SELECT COUNT(), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status'. NON-GROUPABLE: Long text, rich text, encrypted text, compound address/location fields. NON-FILTERABLE: Long text area, rich text, encrypted text, multi-select picklists, blob fields CANNOT be in WHERE. FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) require LIMIT ≤200. ID values need single quotes. Apostrophes use backslash: 'O\'Brien'.

SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT.description: Retrieves all fields (standard and custom) for a Salesforce object with complete metadata including field types, constraints, picklist values, and relationships.

object_name.description: API name of the Salesforce object to describe. Use standard object names (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity) or custom object API names ending in __c.

SALESFORCE_GET_S_OBJECTS_UPDATED.description: Tool to retrieve a list of sObject records that have been updated within a given timeframe. Use when you need to synchronize records or track changes to specific sObject types over a time period.

end.description: End of the timeframe for which to retrieve updated records. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-12-23T23:59:59Z). The date range between start and end cannot exceed 30 days.

start.description: Start of the timeframe for which to retrieve updated records. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-12-23T10:22:26Z). Cannot be more than 30 days ago from the current date.

sobject.description: The API name of the sObject type to query for updated records (e.g., Account, Contact, CustomObject__c).

SALESFORCE_QUERY_ALL.description: Tool to execute SOQL queries including soft-deleted and archived records. Use when you need to query...

SALESFORCE_GET_A_BATCH_OF_RECORDS.description: Tool to retrieve multiple Salesforce records in a single request with customizable field selection. ...

SALESFORCE_GET_OPPORTUNITY.description: Retrieves a specific opportunity by ID from Salesforce, returning all available fields.
